scope: Bounded, read-only original low-level physics/reward-contract audit, plus the requested fast-step signal/telemetry alignment check; not an SAC optimizer, checkpoint, manuscript, macro-handshake, or Table1 evaluator audit.

provenance.anchors: All line numbers are 1-based at the indicated revision; corrected anchors also apply to current for the five audited implementation files and tests/test_physical_contract.py.
provenance.corrected_current_identity: Git blobs are identical for env_low_level.py, physics/{workload,electrical,thermal,bess}.py and test_physical_contract.py. No later research-code change to these files was found.
provenance.manuscript: Not independently read by this physical-contract audit. Parent subsequently verified the original ZIP's camera_ready.tex; see paper_alignment_addendum. No alternate manuscript was used.
provenance.writes: Only this JSON ledger was intentionally written. No repository, attachment, study, Git-ref, remote, or demo edits; no training or full evaluation.

paper_alignment_addendum.verification_owner: Parent audit; accepted source verification, not independently re-run here.
paper_alignment_addendum.source: camera_ready.tex in the original ZIP only

low_level_contract.conclusion: Original command-based throughput code agrees with the original paper. Converting it to actual served_dynamic_work/dynamic_capacity is a changed reward definition coupled to the physics correction, not an original paper/code violation or an incorrect SAC update.

macro_contract_context.classification: Physical-accounting/interpretation inconsistency, not an SAC update error. Macro settlement analysis remains owned by the parent and outside this independent audit.

notation.dt: step duration in seconds; audited default 5 s
notation.N: p_flex_nom_kw, nominal total batch-rack electrical power in kW
notation.M: p_flex_max_kw = 1200 * 75 = 90000 kW for the default plant
notation.Q: queue stored as sums of per-step kW-equivalent work; Q*dt/3600 is its energy-equivalent in kWh at fixed dt, not an instantaneous power measurement
notation.F: gross facility electrical draw in MW, including IT, cooling, auxiliaries, PDU/UPS/transformer losses
notation.B: actual battery AC-side response as exposed by the simulator, in kW; positive discharge
notation.D: demanded response = committed_mw * 1000 * previous observed RegD signal, in kW

findings.classification: confirmed implementation/physical-response inconsistency, not an SAC algorithm bug
findings.claim: Original tracking credits throttle reduction even when the queue serves exactly the same work and electrical load; it also omits negative flex relief during backlog repayment.

equations.original_service: S=min(Q+N,u*M); Q'=Q+N-S; P_flex=S, all in stored kW-equivalent units
equations.corrected_flex_credit: L_new=N-P_flex=A-S kW for valid N>=I; negative on repayment

verified_counterexamples.setup: Empty queue, N=29600 kW, default plant; compare u=0.5 with u=1, equal cooling/BESS/state.
verified_counterexamples.original: Both serve 29600 kW and have identical gross facility power, but u=0.5 receives 14800 kW extra response credit.
verified_counterexamples.corrected_physical_v1: Both serve 20000 dynamic-work kW plus 9600 idle kW; both have zero flex/facility relief.

verified_counterexamples.setup: N=19600 kW held constant; u sequence [0,0,1].
verified_counterexamples.original: P_flex=[0,0,58800] kW; flex credit=[19600,19600,0] kW. Final service exceeds nominal by 39200 kW but receives no negative flex credit.
verified_counterexamples.corrected_physical_v1: P_flex=[9600,9600,39600] kW; flex credit=[10000,10000,-20000] kW. Final full-facility relief was -20026.07711832155 kW in the synthetic microcheck.

findings.status: Fixed in corrected/current physical_v1. Deliberately retained by legacy_v0.
findings.impact: Changes reward_tracking, reported tracking error, frequency-deficit input, and any RMSE/performance settlement derived from them. The sign of metric bias depends on the demanded response; no universal improvement or isolated SAC-gain attribution follows.

findings.claim: Original nominal rack power, including nonzero idle power, is enqueued and can be deferred as if it were batch work.

equations.nominal: N=1200*[8+(75-8)*util^1.4] kW; N=9600 kW at zero utilization
equations.original: Arrival proxy=N; service capacity=u*90000; u=0 sets batch electrical/thermal workload output to zero
equations.corrected: Arrival proxy=max(0,N-9600); service capacity=u*80400; batch draw=9600+served dynamic proxy

verified_counterexample.setup: Zero dynamic utilization, N=9600 kW, empty queue, u=0, dt=5 s.
verified_counterexample.original: Adds 9600 kW-equivalent to backlog despite no dynamic work; emits zero batch draw. This is 13.3333333333 kWh of idle power treated as deferred work for the step.
verified_counterexample.corrected_physical_v1: Arrived work and backlog are zero; 9600 kW idle draw remains.

existing_test_evidence: original tests/test_workload.py:test_throttle_zero_zeroes_flex:151-156 explicitly enshrines the historical zero-flex behavior
findings.status: Fixed when physical_accounting=True, as selected by physical_v1. Standalone WorkloadOrchestrator still defaults to physical_accounting=False for compatibility.
findings.impact: Changes service capacity, queue/SLA penalty and observation, flex power, and thermal loading. Corrected kWh are still energy-equivalent workload proxies, not measured job counts/FLOPs.

findings.claim: Original thermal heat uses raw queued-work power, whereas the electrical model clips inverted utilization and reinstates the server idle floor.

equations.original_electric_A: E_A=clip(P_base_A+S,16000,150000)/1000 MW for default Zone A
equations.corrected_heat: Invert/reconstruct server electrical power first, then feed exactly those reconstructed MW to ThermalTwin and the electrical accounting.

findings.verified_counterexample: P_base_A=6400 kW, P_base_B=10000 kW, N=9600 kW, u=0: original heat input=16.4 MW but electrical IT=26 MW (9.6 MW discrepancy). Corrected physical_v1 heat and electrical IT both equal 26 MW.
findings.qualification: Not a blanket mismatch at every operating point: the inverse/forward round trip agrees when raw zone power is within the allowed rack-power range. Original kW-to-MW division itself is correct.
findings.status: Fixed in physical_v1 through matched heat input and retained idle load; legacy_v0 retains raw heat input.
findings.impact: Can change thermal warnings/faults, cooling demand, feasible actions, episode length and all accumulated metrics. This affects every controller using the environment, not SAC alone.

findings.classification: confirmed response-meter boundary inconsistency plus intentional reference-policy change
findings.claim: Original 'actual response' is not the difference in complete modeled facility/grid electrical draw; it omits liquid-chiller and conversion-loss changes.

equations.corrected_reference: Separate persistent thermal/electrical state, same rigid/nominal flexible trace power and ambient, nominal full service, pump=HVAC=float32(0.7), no BESS; complete facility losses/cooling included.

findings.verified_counterexample: At u=1, pump=HVAC=float32(0.7), B=0 and identical initial state: original reports 450.0006139278412 kW response; corrected physical_v1 reports exactly zero relative to its new reference. The approximately 450 kW difference reflects the intentional pump-reference change from 1.0 to 0.7, not solely a bug fix.
findings.status: Physical_v1 uses the complete modeled facility boundary; legacy_v0 retains the original proxy. Neither counterfactual is a directly measured external utility baseline.
findings.impact: RMSE in kW under the two reference/response definitions is not the same estimand. Gross p_facility_mw excluding BESS is not by itself a bug; using gross power as net import would be a separate evaluator/cost-accounting issue outside this audit.

findings.classification: intentional throughput objective/metric redesign; not a demonstrated SAC or paper-implementation bug
findings.claim: Original rewards commanded throughput/DVFS fraction; corrected physical_v1 rewards served dynamic-work fraction of hardware capacity. The reported throughput_ratio has yet another denominator.

equations.corrected_throughput_metric: throughput_ratio=served_work/(served_work+remaining_backlog), or 1 if available work is zero
equations.backlog_penalty_both: r_backlog=-sla_backlog_penalty*Q'/M; the queue's meaning changes under physical_accounting

verified_counterexamples: N=29600 kW, empty queue, u=0.5 versus 1, alpha=1: identical service but original rewards [0.5,1]; corrected rewards [0.24875621890547264,0.24875621890547264], while corrected throughput_ratio=[1,1].
Zero dynamic work with u=1: original throughput reward=1; corrected reward=0 and corrected throughput_ratio=1.
findings.interpretation: The original source explicitly documents alpha*throttle. Parent verification of original ZIP camera_ready.tex:323-336, especially :326, confirms the paper explicitly defines alpha*theta with matching original weights. Conversion to actual served_dynamic_work/dynamic_capacity is a changed reward definition coupled to the physics correction, not an original paper/code violation or an incorrect SAC update. The config comment 'per unit ... served' is less precise than the actual documented equation.
findings.status: New objective in physical_v1; original definition retained in legacy_v0.
findings.impact: Training targets and summed reward scale change even for identical service. Original and corrected reward totals cannot be compared as if only the policy/optimizer changed.

findings.classification: verified non-finding for the simple BESS backend
findings.claim: Original tracking already uses actual, SOC-limited BESS power, not the requested dispatch.
findings.verified_counterexamples: At dt=5 s and command +/-5 MW: SOC=0.10/0.95 gives zero actual response; SOC=0.105/0.945 gives approximately +/-0.25 MW. Both revisions' tracking response increments equal those actual outputs, not the commands.

existing_test_evidence.execution: All four existing methods in this class passed when invoked directly against each revision's unmodified simple-BESS class: 8 method passes.

findings.qualification: The complete BESS source file is unchanged across original, corrected, and current. This does not certify the optional PySAM adapter or the backend used by historical reported runs.

findings.classification: fast reward/action signal alignment non-finding; confirmed transition-info signal alignment inconsistency
findings.claim: Original tracking is scored against the RegD signal the agent actually observed, not the newly generated next-observation signal. However, the same step's returned info['regd_signal'] contains that next signal, inconsistent with info['delta_p_demanded_kw'].

equations.both_reward_paths: D_t=1000*C_current*regd_observed_t; only afterwards generate gs_next and set _prev_regd_signal for the next action
equations.original_info: info.regd_signal=gs_next.regd_signal, while info.delta_p_demanded_kw refers to regd_observed_t
equations.corrected_physical_info: Save current_grid before advancing; info.regd_signal/current price/load use current_grid, while the returned next observation uses gs_next.

findings.verified_counterexample: Executed the exact source assignments/info expressions with observed RegD=0.25, commitment=10 MW, next RegD=-0.5. Both revisions demand 2500 kW and show -0.5 in the next observation. Original info.regd_signal=-0.5; corrected physical_v1 info.regd_signal=0.25. Thus reconstructing demand from original info.regd_signal yields -5000 kW instead of the correctly scored +2500 kW.
findings.commitment_distinction: Original committed_mw setter at env_low_level.py:269-273 changes the current commitment; observations expose it at :717/:790. If an external macro wrapper changes commitment after the hardware actor's observation, D_t can use an unseen commitment. That is a stale-commitment/interface-ordering issue, not evidence that the fast reward uses the wrong RegD sample. Actual macro ordering was not audited here.
findings.status: Reward already aligned to observed RegD in original. Transition-info mismatch fixed in physical_v1, retained by legacy_v0. No unconditional stale-commitment bug established by this scope.
findings.impact: Original tracking_err_kw itself is computed from the observed signal. The metadata mismatch can corrupt action/signal reconstruction or consumers that reconstruct tracking from info.regd_signal. Returned info LMP likewise comes from the newly generated grid state in original (:636), whereas physical_v1 retains current-grid LMP (:759); Table1 settlement use remains unverified.

remaining_issues_and_limits.claim: PCC voltage still depends on gross facility power/reactive demand, not actual BESS net import.
remaining_issues_and_limits.verified_counterexample: Same fresh plant/action except BESS=0 versus +5 MW actual discharge: v_pcc is 0.9935073774422036 pu in both cases in both revisions. Corrected net import drops 5 MW and tracking response rises 5000 kW, but voltage does not change.
remaining_issues_and_limits.impact: Battery support cannot influence the voltage penalty/fault through this interface. Frequency deficit does include BESS; it is incorrect to claim the entire grid model ignores battery response.

remaining_issues_and_limits.classification: remaining BESS diagnostic inconsistency, not phantom tracking credit
remaining_issues_and_limits.claim: Reported max_charge_mw uses a 0.05 SOC window; actual charge derating uses 0.10.
remaining_issues_and_limits.verified_counterexample: At SOC=0.90, querying with zero power reports max_charge_mw approximately 5; immediately commanding that charge produces approximately -2.5 MW.
remaining_issues_and_limits.impact: The limit diagnostic overstates usable charging near SOC_MAX. The directly audited low-level tracking/reward path uses actual_power_mw and does not consume max_charge_mw, so no direct Table1 impact is established.

remaining_issues_and_limits.classification: remaining deliberate abstractions and compatibility behavior
remaining_issues_and_limits.claim: Corrected work is a dynamic-power-derived energy proxy, not a job/FLOP completion model; queues reset at episode boundaries and legacy semantics remain selectable.
remaining_issues_and_limits.qualification: There is a per-step backlog penalty, but no terminal clearance/payment in the audited low-level reward. Within-episode conservation does not prove service debt is repaid after reset. Holding a 300-second rate across 5-second steps is not itself a 60x work-arrival bug when integrated with dt.
remaining_issues_and_limits.status: Design limitations/compatibility choices, not newly discovered SAC algorithm defects.

remaining_issues_and_limits.classification: conditional original backend/interface issue; source-verified, optional backend not executed
remaining_issues_and_limits.claim: Original BESSModel auto-selects PySAM when importable; corrected physical_v1 explicitly selects _SimpleBESSModel. The PySAM adapter lacks the _age_frac attribute read by low-level info construction.
remaining_issues_and_limits.qualification: Adapters declare different capacities (simple: 15 MWh/5 MW; PySAM-labelled: 150 MWh/50 MW). Native PySAM units/runtime compatibility and historical backend provenance were not established. If the PySAM adapter reaches info construction, the missing _age_frac is incompatible with that access.
remaining_issues_and_limits.status: Physical_v1 avoids this optional path; adapter and legacy path remain unchanged. Do not attribute this condition to reported SAC results without runtime evidence.

table1_and_checkpoint_implications.rmse: A standard RMSE=sqrt(mean((D-R)^2)) in kW changes when R changes from the historical proxy to full counterfactual facility response. Changing the reference cooling policy also changes what is being measured.
table1_and_checkpoint_implications.reward: Step reward includes throughput, tracking, thermal, SOC, frequency, voltage and backlog components. The throughput objective and queue semantics change; reward totals are not directly interchangeable across simulation modes.
table1_and_checkpoint_implications.revenue: No Table1 evaluator or macro settlement source was audited. Any revenue depending on tracking performance inherits the changed R/error definition. Physical net energy should use (F-B/1000)*dt_hours MWh, not gross F; whether the original Table1 evaluator does so is outside this scope.
table1_and_checkpoint_implications.interface_evidence: Both bare low-level environments expose four action levers and build 18 observations: original env_low_level.py:422-443,686-717; corrected:492-517,829-860. This alone does not establish compatibility of a particular Table2 checkpoint, wrapper, VecNormalize state, mode metadata, or macro-vs-low-level model.
recomputation_options: Evaluating a corrected policy under the original contract would be a new-policy result on the historical proxy task, not recovery of the original trained SAC policy/result. Exact source or verified legacy behavior, checkpoint loading and normalization compatibility remain prerequisites.

Evaluating under physical_v1 would produce a corrected-physics Table1-style comparison, not literal reproduction of original Table1 metrics. Re-evaluate comparator rows under the same contract, reference, traces, scenarios and horizons.
Do not replace only the original SAC row with a physical_v1 score beside unchanged historical baseline rows, or describe the changed throughput objective as an SAC implementation repair.
table1_and_checkpoint_implications.causal_limit: No isolated causal effect on reported SAC gains was measured or claimed. No checkpoint was loaded, no policy trained, and no Table1/Table2 full evaluation was run.

validation.method: Read exact git-show blobs; compared corrected/current blob identity. Executed unmodified step-method bodies extracted in memory with AST, using synthetic valid workload state, default 5-second plant parameters, simple BESS, static grid/weather, and an observation stub. Gym inheritance/imports and reset/data-loading paths were bypassed; these were isolated contract checks, not end-to-end environment evaluations.
validation.microcheck_results: All final assertions passed: unused-capacity no-power-change, original/corrected flex credit, idle heat/electrical balance, corrected work conservation (residual 3.55e-15 kWh), repayment sign, actual BESS boundary response, unchanged voltage under BESS dispatch, and legacy credit retention. Additional exact-source statement/expression checks verified observed-signal scoring versus next-signal telemetry in original and corrected versions.
validation.bounded_work: 27 low-level step calls across fresh synthetic states; no synthetic sequence longer than three steps.
validation.existing_tests_executed: Directly invoked the four original and four corrected TestBESSDeratingFix methods, with no pytest fixtures/files; all eight passed.
validation.existing_tests_read_only: Physical-contract tests and directly relevant original workload tests were inspected and cited, not run as a pytest suite.
validation.dependencies: Used existing system Python 3.10, NumPy and YAML. Pandas/Gymnasium were unavailable there; no dependencies were installed and no temporary files or test fixtures were created by the audit code.
